name: Cosmic microwave background
meaning: The cosmic microwave background as Planck's 2018 SMICA map shows it, drawn on the sphere it left from: the surface of last scattering, at the comoving distance of redshift 1089.80 in the Planck 2018 cosmology, 13.9 Gpc (45 billion light-years) away. Seen from outside, it is the edge of the observable universe.

colourTable.basis: The Planck collaboration's style-guide colour table for CMB maps (the paperplots repository of its figure style guide), 256 colours from blue through parchment to red.
colourTable.gammaBasis: Presentation choice, picked from renders (full colour, colour at 60% and 45%, gamma 1.6 and 2.2): each colour channel of the table raised to the power 1.6, as the star dots are, so the table's cream middle, where most of the sky sits, darkens most and the ball stops glaring beside the dots while its reds and blues keep their colour.

range.basis: Plus and minus 300 microkelvin around the mean, the range of the Planck 2018 CMB figures; the few hotter or colder pixels take the table's end colours.

radius.basis: z* = 1089.80 ± 0.21, the redshift of last scattering in Planck 2018 VI, Table 2, TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO (the parameters Astropy's Planck18 carries); its comoving distance is the sphere's radius.

mesh.basis: Presentation choice: the planets' standard sphere, 16 latitude bands of 32 cells (11.25 degrees each), ICRS north up, the top and bottom bands closed by round polar caps: 450 planar patches, each 64 texels on a side (about 0.18 degrees per texel at the equator, coarser than the map's 5 arcminute beam), each texel the mean of 2 by 2 samples.

limb.basis: Presentation choice: the last-scattering surface has no limb that anyone could see from outside it, so this is not a measurement. It is the linear limb law, I(mu)/I(1) = 1 - u(1 - mu), drawn as the bodies' limb plates are, with u = 0.6 picked from renders so the ball reads as round.

cutaway.basis: Presentation choice: the sphere opens its ICRS northern hemisphere so the galaxies and quasars inside it show. While it is open, the inside of the southern half is drawn at 55% opacity so it reads as the inside wall, and the outer shell at 85% so the inside stands out. Nothing is cut in the data.

lenses.label: Cut open
lenses.title: The cosmic microwave background, cut open
lenses.summary: Planck's map of the oldest light, with its northern half open so the galaxies and quasars inside show.
lenses.description: Planck's 2018 SMICA map of the cosmic microwave background, drawn on the sphere the light left from, 13.9 Gpc away. The ICRS northern half is left out of the drawing so the inside shows: the far wall's inside at 55% opacity, the rest of the shell at 85%. The opening is a way of looking, not a feature of the sky.

lenses.label: Full sphere
lenses.title: The whole cosmic microwave background
lenses.summary: Planck's map of the oldest light on the whole sphere it left from: the edge of the observable universe, seen from outside.
lenses.description: Planck's 2018 SMICA map of the cosmic microwave background, drawn on the sphere the light left from, 13.9 Gpc away, as a closed shell. Seen from outside it hides everything inside it.

preview.basis: Presentation choice: each dataset's picture is the sphere seen from far away along a line 30 degrees above the ICRS equator at right ascension 0h, north up, drawn each pixel the mean of 3 by 3 rays, from the same map, limb law and cutaway opacities the page uses, over black.
